name: Port of Alicante – Stanbrook and the last refugees
story: As the Republic collapsed in March 1939, tens of thousands of Republican soldiers, officials and families converged on Alicante, hoping for evacuation by sea. On 28 March the British collier Stanbrook, under Captain Archibald Dickson, sailed for Oran carrying about 2,600–3,000 people, far beyond her capacity. Very few ships came after her. Between 15,000 and 20,000 people were left on the quays. Italian troops of the Littorio Division and Nationalist forces took the port, and on 1 April some of those trapped killed themselves rather than surrender. The rest were marched to the Los Almendros field and then to Albatera. The Generalitat Valenciana now marks 28 March as a day of remembrance.
see: Today a modern ferry and leisure port. A plaque to the Stanbrook's crew stands on the quayside (it was torn off once by vandals) and a street is named after the ship.
plan: Walk the waterfront from the Explanada. The plaque's exact position is not confirmed, so ask at the port tourist office. Combine with Los Almendros, 2 km north.

boxes.text: Stanbrook passengers are given as 2,638 by some sources and 'about 3,000' by others. Estimates of those left behind range from 15,000 to more than 20,000.
